# Eight lessons — Weeks13–14
Unit4 full-course consolidation after Weeks11–12 review; no project spillover/new summative tasks. Year12 Units3–4 integrated, earlier foundations revisited where diagnosed. Typically50–55minutes per lesson; adapt to actual timetable.
Week13 L1:30min16mark diagnostic,15min criterion/evidence review,5–10min two priorities. L2:5min retrieval,15min Python/algorithm/OOP modelled repair,25min independent relevant tasks,5–10min exit. L3:5min retrieval,15min SQL/design repair,25min fresh seed tasks,5–10min feedback. L4:5min retrieval,15min network/security boundary comparison,25min case/address practice,5–10min explanation. Teacher uses these common clinics to establish prerequisites; not every long station is completed by every learner.
Week14 L1: priority1 clinic with teacher feedback and fresh independent attempt. L2:priority2 clinic same pattern. L3: short mixed transfer(T6), peer/teacher evidence review, changed task; no extra test weighting. L4: delayed priority retries, record demonstrated/needsretry/notyet evidenced, schedule small revision tasks for Weeks15–16 and remaining support. A delayed retry uses a later lesson, not a promised homework deadline.
Teacher can reteach the common gap and assign extension to demonstrated learners. Each chosen station sequence: identify cause -> one worked step -> guided variation -> independent fresh variation -> explanation -> delayed retry. Pack tasks are a menu sampled to fit allocation, not compulsory extra homework. Avoid arbitrary grades/automated mastery thresholds.
Answers/reference code openly downloadable; not secure assessment material. Visual course-symbol verification and actual learner work still need review. No real networks/personal data or operational system changes.
